security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, trap handlers (page fault, misaligned access, illegal instruction, etc.) read stval/mtval/htval to obtain the faulting address and use it for memory access, fixup, or signal delivery (si_addr), but the kernel does not account for whether pointer masking was enabled for the faulting privilege mode. When pointer masking was applicable at the time of the exception, the hardware has already applied the ignore transformation to the address in *tval, so the kernel receives a masked/transformed address rather than the raw effective address. If the kernel then performs address-space operations (e.g., comparing against VM bounds, walking page tables, or passing to userspace via siginfo) based on this masked address without understanding the masking context, it operates on a semantically different address than the one that triggered the fault.
security_spec.summary: Kernel trap handlers reading *tval CSRs must determine whether pointer masking was applicable to the faulting context before using the value as an address; unconditionally treating *tval as the raw faulting address when PM was active yields a transformed address, leading to incorrect page table walks, wrong si_addr in signals, and corrupted KVM guest state.
